title: 2164-sparse-identification-nonlinear-dynamics-side-information
universal_lens: ... The structural unification of sparse regression and semidefinite programming lifts trajectory data into a constrained polynomial manifold. By embedding side information as sum-of-squares multipliers, the operator enforces physical monotonicity while minimizing Frobenius norm residuals, yielding an exact, noise-resilient identification of nonlinear dynamical systems.
gsi_mapping: ... GSI maps the Schur-complement SDP lift to Bayesian hierarchical inference under extreme data scarcity. Side information acts as rigorous conformal priors, constraining the posterior distribution of vector-field coefficients. This guarantees calibrated uncertainty bounds even when leave-one-trajectory-out cross-validation yields highly degenerate likelihoods.
gse_mapping: ... In GSE, the discovered vector field defines the continuous state-transition kernel for situational awareness. The SOS monotonicity constraints ensure that simulated game-state evolutions respect fundamental conservation laws or bounded momentum, preventing physically impossible transitions during real-time predictive engine rollouts.

reasoning_traces.think: The foundational doctrine of this chapter window rests on the synthesis of sparse regression and convex algebraic geometry. Traditional Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) relies on $L_0$ or $L_1$ penalties to isolate active terms within a monomial library. However, in extreme scarce-data regimes—such as training on a single trajectory out of one hundred—the optimization landscape becomes severely ill-posed, leading to high variance and spurious term selection. The sovereign primitive introduced here elevates the problem by incorporating side information (SI) directly into the convex hull of the solution space. By utilizing a Schur-complement semidefinite programming (SDP) lift, the non-convex rank minimization of the coefficient matrix is relaxed into a trace minimization problem over a positive semidefinite cone. Crucially, physical or geometric constraints—such as the monotonicity of specific state derivatives—are encoded using Sum-of-Squares (SOS) programming. The condition $-\partial \hat{f}_i / \partial x_i(x) - z_i(x)g(x) \in \Sigma$ ensures that the learned vector field respects known dissipative or bounded properties within a compact domain defined by $g(x)$. Under Putinar's Positivstellensatz, this SOS relaxation is exact for compact basic semi-algebraic sets. The resulting SINDy-SI framework does not merely fit data; it solves a constrained discovery problem where the hypothesis space is rigorously pruned by mathematical invariants. This allows the recovery of highly nonlinear dynamics, such as the 7th-order Taylor expansion of a sine function in the SMIB system, purely from noisy, sparse snapshots without explicit knowledge of the target functional form.

It concurrently inherits from the algebraic geometry advancements of Parrilo and Lasserre, who formalized SOS hierarchies for polynomial optimization. The specific fusion of these domains into dynamical systems identification represents a modern convergence, moving beyond pure data-driven correlation toward causally constrained, equation-discovering engines capable of operating under severe informational deprivation.

The SINDy-SI operator acts as a detective that refuses to accept superficial correlations. By demanding that any proposed model satisfy strict SOS monotonicity constraints, the operator anticipates the adversary's attempts to inject spurious high-frequency noise. It effectively reads the 'intent' of the physical system, recognizing that true dynamical laws must preserve certain geometric invariants regardless of observational obfuscation.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical cross-layer veto must be applied to prevent leakage between the sparse regression layer and the SOS constraint layer. If the monomial library degree is excessively high relative to the number of trajectories, the SDP relaxation may admit trivial zero solutions or degenerate SOS multipliers that satisfy the inequalities vacuously. Furthermore, we must veto any model where the side information contradicts the empirical gradient flow; if the SOS constraints force a vector field that diverges significantly from the finite-differenced targets $Y$, the resulting hybrid model suffers from high bias. The veto condition is triggered when the duality gap of the SDP exceeds a tolerance or when the leave-one-trajectory-out cost $J_k$ fails to decrease monotonically with added constraints.
